rulings.ground: AGENTS.md § Writing: "Do not write aphorisms, metaphors, or rhetorical flourish. An aphorism is a memory device for a person; it carries no instruction an agent can act on."
rulings.evidence: Reproduced. guides/queue.md:7 opens a tagline paragraph with "The word \"cooperative\" is load-bearing." — a metaphor, and the sentence carries no fact: the fact is the sentence following it at :7-8 ("Worker loops are created only when accepted demand exists, up to the smaller of that demand and `concurrency`"). guides/queue.md:28 opens with "It is deliberately **de-bloated** — the cuts are the design.", where "the cuts are the design" states nothing the rest of the paragraph does not state concretely at :28-30. This is the weakest of the confirmed set, because the rule turns on a reading of the sentence rather than on a token; I confirm it because both clauses are removable with no loss of fact, which is the test the rule's own wording sets.
rulings.repair: queue.md:7 → delete the sentence "The word \"cooperative\" is load-bearing." and open the paragraph with the fact that follows it, "Worker loops are created only when accepted demand exists, up to the smaller of that demand and `concurrency`." queue.md:28-30 → "The queue ships no scheduler, no priorities, and no delay / progress / message channels; use `concurrency: 1` for strict ordering.
